sources.citation: Shalabh, Sampling Theory, MTH 417 lecture notes, Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur; Chapters 1, 2, 4, 7, 9 and 10.
sources.authority: Author/institution course notes linked from the IIT Kanpur instructor course page.
anchors: Ch. 1: population, census, samples, study variables and survey error.
Ch. 2: SRSWOR/SRSWR, sample mean/total, finite-population correction, indicator inclusion probabilities, variance and normal-based inference.
Ch. 4: stratified SRS estimators, variances and proportional/Neyman/cost allocations.
Ch. 7: varying-probability sampling, Hansen–Hurwitz, Horvitz–Thompson, pair inclusion probabilities and Yates–Grundy variance.
Ch. 9: one-stage cluster sampling, cluster-level estimators, intracluster correlation and design effects.
Ch. 10: two-stage/subsampling estimators, variance decomposition and allocation.
source_caveats: Chapter 2 p. 14 prints a positive sign for covariance of distinct SRSWOR inclusion indicators. The correct value is πij−πiπj=−n(N−n)/(N²(N−1)); the printed sign contradicts the displayed probabilities.

Chapter 2 pp. 17–21 treats the sample mean as exactly normal under a normal finite population. A fixed finite population yields a discrete randomization distribution; exact normal inference requires a superpopulation model or an approximation.
Chapter 9 p. 7 says ρ=0 means there is no error. It means no intracluster-correlation design-effect inflation; ordinary sampling error remains.

anchors: §5.3.3.2: nuisance-factor blocking, within-block comparisons and randomization.
§5.3.3.3–.4: orthogonal factorial columns, factorial interactions, fractional generators, alias structure and resolution.

§7.2.2.2: sample size depends on α, β, variance and shift; unknown-variance calculation needs iteration.
source_caveats: The D-opt section gives an applied algorithm and criterion, not a proof of the equivalence theorem; that proof must be supplied from log-determinant concavity and a directional-derivative argument.

The section recommends fixed-time center-point control runs. Keep them randomized subject to the monitoring constraint where feasible and address run-order trends explicitly; deterministic time order can confound treatment effects with drift.
